title: Hosted API fidelity-on-demand playbook (PRD draft)
content:
Summary:
This draft defines a 'fidelity-on-demand' approach for the Hosted API: clients receive compact, low-latency partial outputs by default and can progressively request richer structured content or tool-resolved results. The goal is to reduce tail latency and token cost for common fast-path use cases while enabling deterministic, resumable upgrades to higher-fidelity outputs when applications require them.

Problem statement:
- Many customers want sub-200ms first-token latency for UX-critical interactions (autocomplete, suggestion bubbles) but also need structured or tool-backed results for final actions (bookings, purchases, DB writes). Current monolithic streaming and tool-call flows force either:
  * Always compute expensive tool calls and full structured conversion (higher latency/cost), or
  * Provide a cheap unstructured string (low utility for downstream automation).
- SDK ergonomics are inconsistent: clients either re-run expensive calls or implement brittle heuristics to detect when to fetch more detailed outputs.
- Observability and retry semantics for mid-stream tool calls are unclear — tool failures often lead to user-visible partials with no clear recovery path.

Goals (measurable):
- Default first-token latency <= 200ms median for small prompts (<= 256 context), 95th <= 400ms.
- Reduce average per-request cost by enabling early cheap responses in 60% of interactive sessions.
- Provide a deterministic, resumable upgrade path from low-fidelity to high-fidelity outputs with idempotent semantics.
- Expose a small, ergonomic SDK surface for request-time fidelity controls and local fallbacks.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing streaming protocol; this augments it with explicit fidelity layers and upgrade APIs.
- Full offline execution of tool calls in the SDK.

User personas and example flows:
- Product UX engineer (mobile): wants a fast preview text for autocomplete, then a richer structured object if user taps 'confirm'.
- Automation engineer (backend): needs machine-readable JSON for downstream pipelines; must be able to request guaranteed tool-resolution for critical writes.
- Platform integrator (enterprise): wants clear cost/latency tradeoffs and audit logs per fidelity escalation.

High-level concept: fidelity layers and incremental hydration
- Base layer (fast): minimal token output, plain text or minimal jsonl, generated without invoking toolchain or complex structured parsers. Streams quickly.
- Structured layer (hydrate-json): an optional second pass that returns a validated JSON schema (e.g., action contract) derived from the same prompt; may run additional parsing passes but does not invoke external tools.
- Tool-resolve layer (tools-resolve): when requested, the model will trigger configured tool calls (search, calendar, payments) and return a final resolved object. Tool calls may be executed synchronously (blocking) or asynchronously with a follow-up event.
- Each layer is addressable and resumable via a stable request id/continuation token.

API semantics (sketch) — plain language, not a spec file:
- client POST /v1/generate with body: prompt, fidelity: ["base" | "structured" | "resolve"], resume_token (optional), session_id (optional), stream=true|false, prefer_latency_budget_ms (optional).
- Responses for stream=true: initial frames include a 'fidelity' header: 'base'. When the server flushes the base output, it includes an optional 'upgrade_hint' describing expected cost and ETA to produce structured output.
- If client wants structured output it calls same endpoint with fidelity=structured and resume_token set to value received from initial run. The system guarantees deterministic derivation from the same model seed + prompt when possible (subject to model nondeterminism caveats).
- For tool resolution, fidelity=resolve triggers tool orchestration. The server returns either a blocking final object or an async ticket and event endpoint (webhook/poll) if tool latency exceeds configured budget.
- Resume tokens encode minimal state: model version id, prompt hash, base-output-checksum, and server-side checkpoint pointer. Tokens are opaque to clients but durable for 48 hours by default.

SDK ergonomics (principles):
- Minimal surface: two new high-level helpers: generateFidelityBase() which streams the cheap preview, and escalateFidelity(resumeToken, target) which fetches structured or tool-resolved results.
- Backpressure & cancellation: streaming helpers must expose a cancel() and a suggestLowerFidelity() signal; SDK maps this to prefer_latency_budget_ms to influence server scheduling.
- Local spec validation: the SDK includes lightweight validators for common structured schemas so clients can pre-validate fields and decide whether to escalate.
- Retry & idempotency: escalateFidelity should be idempotent; SDK will attach a client-generated idempotency token when re-issuing escalations.

Observability and instrumentation:
- Server-side: log per-request fidelity transitions, time spent in each layer, tool call latencies, and cost estimate fields. Emit traces with spans: base-gen, structure-parse, tool-orchestration.
- Client SDK telemetry: surface timing from first-byte to base-complete, escalate latency, and boolean flags indicating whether an escalation was necessary.
- Console dashboards: add a fidelity breakdown view (percent of requests that stop at base vs structured vs resolved), median latencies by fidelity, and per-tool success rates.

Failure modes and graceful degradation:
- Tool failure during resolve: return a structured object with 'tools':[{"name":..., "status":"failed","fallback":"suggested-text"}] and a boolean 'resolved': false.
- Expired resume_token: return 410 with a short re-run recommendation and a deterministic recompute hint.
- Partial determinism: if structured layer cannot be deterministically derived, server returns 'determinism': 'best-effort' and a confidence score.

Security & compliance notes:
- Tool-resolve layer may access customer connectors (calendar, crm). Ensure KMS key usage is logged at tool-exec time.
- Resume tokens must not leak PII; strip user tokens and store only prompt hashes in tokens.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiments): internal feature-flag behind opt-in for a subset of customers; measure base-first latency and up-sell rates.
- Phase 1 (beta): expose SDK helpers, event webhooks for async tool-resolve, default resume_token lifetime 48h. Invite 10 customers (PLG growth cohort).
- Phase 2 (public): turn on for hosted-api tenants with opt-out; add console fidelity dashboards and per-tenant cost controls.

Metrics to watch:
- % requests served at base only vs escalated
- Median/95th latency for base and structured stages
- Mean tokens per session and cost reduction vs baseline
- Tool success/failure rates and rollback frequency

Open questions / tradeoffs:
1) Deterministic rehydration vs improved model quality: do we prioritize bit-for-bit repeatability for resume, or allow small sampling for better structured outputs? Proposal: best-effort determinism with explicit confidence and a strict fallback path.
2) Server-side vs client-driven tool execution: Should server auto-execute low-risk tools during structured passes? Risk: unexpected side-effects. Proposal: default to client-initiated resolve, but enable opt-in auto-resolve for enterprise tenants after explicit permission.
3) Token format and lifetime: 48h is a starting point; need legal/arch input for retention policy.

Implementation notes for eng teams:
- Serving-runtime: add a checkpointing hook after base-gen that can save KV-cache and prompt-hash pointers.
- Orchestration: tool-resolver must accept a cost/latency budget and choose sync vs async invocation.
- SDKs: implement generateFidelityBase as streaming-first helper; escalateFidelity will be a simple wrapper that posts resume_token + target fidelity.

Appendix — UX examples and short transcript:
- Mobile autocomplete: client calls generateFidelityBase() -> streams short suggestion (80ms). User taps confirm -> escalateFidelity(resumeToken, "resolve") -> server either returns resolved booking object (sync, 350ms) or returns job ticket + webhook.
- Admin automation: server-to-server calls default to fidelity=resolve. SDKs skip base layer and use structured fast-path helpers for bulk jobs.

Next steps & action items:
- Product: align on determinism policy and token lifetime (owner: Priya Rao, due 2025-10-10).
- Eng (serving-runtime): spike resume-token checkpointing and cost-estimate hints (owner: Martin Gomez, due 2025-11-01).
- Eng (sdk): prototype JS helper surface and cancellation semantics (owner: Evan Liu, due 2025-10-20).

Notes to reviewers:
This doc is intentionally implementation-sketchy. Looking for feedback on API shape, SDK ergonomics, and failure-handling semantics. Please add comments inline or link to JIRA-PRD-4132 for major design decisions.
